commission_independent_closing_02.text: The final physical goods were three pieces: two disputed coats and one strap with a loose loop. Yue counted them with the keeper and outside witness present. They were not three missing containers. Their descriptions matched the retained opening inventory and later exception sheets. The remaining released goods had signed outward records. Separating those categories let the final arithmetic say something more useful than that the numbers seemed reassuring.

commission_independent_closing_03.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_03.text: Twenty-four mats had been released, along with sixteen coats and eleven straps. Those fifty-one accepted outward pieces joined the three retained pieces to account for the opening fifty-four. The original twelve containers had been opened, emptied or reassigned as holding wrappers during the week. The witness checked individual pieces and attributable receipts rather than demanding twelve full packages be present at the end of a receiving job.

commission_independent_closing_04.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_04.text: The two coat claimants had reached no allocation agreement through the cooperative's office. A new written holding instruction named the keeper as the receiving custodian after Yue's term. It permitted continued dry-condition checks and prohibited release without the office's decision. Yue placed the instruction beside the coats. The final sheet reported unresolved allocation. It did not turn preservation into a verdict about who deserved them most.

commission_independent_closing_05.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_05.text: The supplier's return instruction for the defective strap remained current. The piece would be collected at its next scheduled visit, with the keeper recording that actual movement when it occurred. Yue entered no future return among this week's completed releases. The final account could make the next step easier without claiming it already done. The strap's condition and custody were present facts; the planned collection remained a plan.

commission_independent_closing_06.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_06.text: The witness asked whether the held pieces meant the commission had failed. Yue answered that her accepted task was attributable receiving, sorting and reporting exceptions. Those pieces showed exceptions correctly preserved. The keeper agreed and pointed to the contract. This was no permission to stop early when work became difficult. It was the named distinction between completing a receiving term and obtaining answers outside its authority.

commission_independent_closing_07.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_07.text: The porter checked the handover by standing where tomorrow's replacement worker would stand. He asked which sheet described the held strap and who could authorize a coat release. Yue directed him to the actual documents without summarizing their decisions from memory. The keeper then took the board and answered the same questions. The handover mattered because the next morning would arrive after Yue had put her coat on and left.

commission_independent_closing_08.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_08.text: They counted the base materials purchased with twelve copper. Used tags and wrapping were accounted for through the receiving work; the remaining dry supplies stayed with the court. The receipts named delivered goods, not an imaginary cash remainder equal to whatever happened to be unused. A sheet could remain unused after being honestly purchased. The witness wanted its location and responsible keeper, rather than a story in which the supplier had never delivered it.

commission_independent_closing_09.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_09.text: The outside witness accepted both the opening comparison and the final reconciliation and received the agreed eight copper. He had not been paid to certify that no error occurred. His receipt named the observations and source checks he actually performed. Yue thought this distinction made the fee more valuable. The court had bought independent attention to its account, including the part that showed her wrong tick.

commission_independent_closing_10.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_10.text: The porter completed his eighth morning and received his last three copper, making twenty-four for eight dates. The receiving keeper's eight mornings totalled sixteen at two each. Their attendance sheets did not include each other's tasks or the independently purchased supplementary service. The account showed people earning money through the work they had actually supplied. Yue could see the whole arrangement without treating her own wage as its only meaningful line.

commission_independent_closing_11.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_11.text: The supplementary page recorded the one accepted twelve-copper service, its actual supplied dates or delivered materials, and the two declined offers. No second service appeared in the final total. Forty-eight for Yue, twenty-four for the porter, sixteen for the keeper, twelve for base materials, eight for the witness and twelve for the selected service exhausted the new one hundred and twenty. No old crossing deficit or training surplus moved into the account.

commission_independent_closing_12.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_12.text: The keeper accepted Yue's eighth performed morning and paid its six copper. Forty-eight had now reached her across eight dated mornings. Her own meals and lodging remained personal expenses outside the court's appropriation. Yue counted the wage coins, then signed the actual receipt. She had wanted the total since reading the offer. Receiving it now felt different because every part could be traced to a morning she remembered.

commission_independent_closing_13.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_13.text: The completed handover, retained exceptions and witnessed reconciliation earned one further point of responsibility practice, recorded once after the work. The specialist qualification columns stayed blank. Her fifth stage retained four pairs, and her shoulder still required the limits under which the term had been performed. She had advanced as an ordinary worker entrusted with receiving and materials stewardship within this court's accepted scope.

commission_independent_closing_14.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_14.text: The keeper prepared a reference naming eight paid mornings, checked individual and container counts, attributable correction of a move error, the selected improvement and final custody handover. It did not call Yue a kiln inspector, archive conservator or survey officer. Yue asked the keeper to keep the words about the retained error. An employer who saw only the tidy last arithmetic would learn less about the practice she could actually bring.

commission_independent_closing_15.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_15.text: The porter wanted to buy her a meal to celebrate the closing. Yue accepted only after he said he meant an invitation, not another expense he expected the court to repay. They sat under a repair shop's awning while rain reached the edge of their table. He told her his daughter had chosen one of the released patched coats. The court had received no special instruction for her; he sounded pleased that she had liked the one allocated.

commission_independent_closing_16.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_16.text: Yue asked whether he would use the movement aid after she left. He said he would use the part that helped and tell the keeper when the floor arrangement changed. She liked that answer more than a promise to preserve every mark she had drawn. Their shared work was not a monument to her improvement. It was a procedure owned by the people who would have to make it function in the next ordinary week.

commission_independent_closing_17.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_17.text: A cooperative member came past carrying the child in the blue-patched coat. Yue recognized the cloth and almost remembered the opening parcel before she remembered the person. The child showed her a button sewn on since collection. The work had passed beyond the receiving record into someone else's decisions. That was a satisfying ending for a parcel. It was not evidence that the two coats still held should have been released without their own permission.

commission_independent_closing_18.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_18.text: Later, Yue copied the reference into her permitted work summary and put the court's private notes back where they belonged. Her own page said what she had done, where its sources remained and how an employer could request confirmation. The old crossing account retained its losses. Earlier qualifications or their blank spaces retained their truth. This new account belonged beside them, without being tasked to heal every uncomfortable page before it.

commission_independent_closing_19.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_19.text: The keeper offered to notify her if another bounded term became available. Yue agreed to receive actual terms, without reserving an unpaid stretch of future mornings. A recommendation could make an offer more likely; it did not make its dates or wages exist. She wrote her current contact address and an earliest available date. The act looked small compared with signing a lasting appointment, and fit the freedom she had wanted to keep.

commission_independent_closing_20.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_20.text: On the walk back, she saw workers taking the ordinary morning notice down. The court's new week would use its own people, money and clearances. Yue felt both relief and the slight loss of having no task waiting there tomorrow. Independent work had taught her how to become useful in a place without making that place owe her permanence. She tightened her coat with her uninjured hand and kept the reference dry.

commission_independent_closing_21.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_closing_21.text: At the receiving appointed for completed commissions, Yue carried her dated reference and wage receipts rather than the court's private ledger. Her next application could describe a tested ordinary logistics practice: count, preserve exceptions, coordinate lawful movements and leave a usable handover. It could not claim any unperformed specialist training. She reached the table prepared to answer for the work she had done and to read whatever new promise might come next.

commission_independent_entry.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_entry.text: The covered tally court stood behind a row of repair shops, where the roof caught rain without pretending to keep the whole town dry. Yue arrived carrying her work book inside her coat. At the gate, a porter was lifting a ramp from a puddle. She waited until he had somewhere firm to set it before asking for the receiving keeper. A request could be urgent without becoming the most important weight in somebody else's hands.

commission_independent_recovery_choice.speaker: lin_yue
commission_independent_recovery_choice.text: The affected coat bundles remain held until the record is checked. I can reconstruct the movement through the retained sheets and parcel ties, or through a supervised physical sequence with the porter. Both preserve the original mistake and leave the two recipients' dispute to its authorized office. I want the correction to leave a practical aid someone else can use when I am away.

choices.text: Compare retained sheets and ties; build a usable paper index.
Reconstruct the move with the porter; test a floor movement aid.

commission_independent_service_choice.speaker: lin_yue
commission_independent_service_choice.text: The twelve-copper supplementary allocation can purchase one improvement. A covered rack gives dry holding space for four mornings; paired labels preserve clearer outward evidence; three later windows give approved collectors access after their own work. Each has an accountable supplier and leaves the other needs with the ordinary arrangements. I will recommend one actual service and name what this week will still have to manage.

choices.text: Hire the temporary covered rack for mornings four through seven.
Buy paired labels and checked outward receipt copies.
Fund three bounded later receiving windows.

commission_independent_service_result_ga.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_service_result_ga.text: The next two mornings tested the supplementary arrangement actually selected and supplied. The court's service page retained its accepted offer, dates and receiving evidence. Yue would report the observed benefit of that particular work, together with the weaknesses it had left to ordinary precautions. An absent selection record could support no named service consequence by assumption; only attributable pages could enter the commission's final account.

commission_independent_recovery_result_g.speaker: narrator
commission_independent_recovery_result_g.text: On the eighth morning, the outside witness requested the practical evidence behind the corrected coat record. Its form followed the recovery Yue had actually performed. A preserved choice could direct him to the tested paper index or the tested movement aid. Without that record, neither particular aid would be credited by inference; he would examine only available source sheets and observed work before accepting the final reconciliation.
